rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muhammad invited Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and Kaʿb ibn Asad to Islam, they denied him, claiming God sent no book after Moses; Muqatil says their denial prompted the verse.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن كعب بن الأشرف، وكعب بن أسيد، لما دعاهما النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That Book” means this Qurʾān, the book the Jews rejected.
rows.anchor: بمعنى هذا الكتاب الذى كفرت به اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no doubt that the Qurʾān came from God and that He revealed it to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: لا شك فيه أنه من الله جاء، وهو أنزله على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān guides people away from error, and the God-fearing are those who avoid associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: هذا القرآن { هدى } من الضلالة { للمتقين } من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to people means the hypocrites and Jews, whom Muqatil calls to worship and affirm the oneness of their Lord.
rows.anchor: يعنى المنافقين واليهود وحدوا ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the addressees when they were nothing, as He created the nations before them.
rows.anchor: ولم تكونوا شيئا، { والذين من قبلكم } من الأمم الخالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla here means “so that”; reflecting on creation should lead people to avoid shirk and affirm God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: الشرك وتوحدوا الله عز وجل إذا تفكرتم فى خلقكم وخلق الذين من قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth a spread-out carpet and the sky a roof.
rows.anchor: يعنى بساطا، { والسماء بنآء } ، يعنى سقفا

words: وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزْقًۭا لَّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain from heaven brings varieties of fruit from the earth as provision for people.
rows.anchor: يقول: فأخرج بالمطر من الأرض أنواعا

words: فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًۭا وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not assign God partners: people know these signs are all His work, so Muqatil asks how they can worship anyone else.
rows.anchor: وأنتم تعلمون } [آية: 22] أن هذا الذى ذكر كله من صنعه، فكيف تعبدون غيره

words: سُبْحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are the angels, who glorify God and acknowledge that they know only what He taught them.
rows.anchor: قالوا } قالت الملائكة { سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا

words: لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ
rows.speaker: الله عز وجل
rows.claim: God challenges the angels for claiming knowledge of what had not yet been created or seen when they do not know even what they see.
rows.anchor: قال الله عز وجل لهم: كيف تدعون العلم فيما لم يخلق بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the occasion as the Roman Tyakhus ibn Babilis and his people, Christians who prevented worship at Jerusalem’s temple.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى الطياخوس بن ببليس الرومى ومن معه من أهل الروم

words: مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God’s mosques” refers to Jerusalem’s temple, and remembering God’s name there means affirming His oneness.
rows.anchor: يعنى بيت المقدس أن يصلى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Romans defeated the Jews, killing and enslaving them, wrecked Jerusalem, dumped corpses there, and slaughtered pigs in the temple.
rows.anchor: فقتلوهم وسبوهم وخربوا بيت المقدس، وألقوا فيه الجيف، وذبحوا فيه الخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under a second Roman ruler, Ttusir ibn Sanabatous or Stephanos, the Romans again killed Jews and destroyed the temple; it remained unrestored until Muslims rebuilt it under ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: ططسر بن سناباتوس، ويقال: اصطفانوس، فقتلهم وخرب بيت المقدس

words: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلَّا خَآئِفِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Romans should not enter the holy land after Muhammad’s mission except in fear; a Roman entering Jerusalem must come disguised, and is punished if caught.
rows.anchor: يعنى الأرض المقدسة إذ بعث محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil describes their worldly abasement as Muslim forces killing combatants and enslaving descendants in Constantinople, Rome, and Amorium; their afterlife punishment is fire.
rows.anchor: إن لم تقتل مقاتلتهم وتسب ذراريهم بأيدى المسلمين

words: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees Muhammad gazing toward heaven and promises to turn him toward his desired qibla because the Kaʿba was dearer to him than Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: يعنى نرى أنك تديم نظرك إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Turn” means change direction, and shatr means toward; worshippers are to face the Kaʿba in prayer.
rows.anchor: فول } ، يعنى فحول { وجهك شطر } ، يعني تلقاء

words: وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command applies to all worshippers: turn toward the Kaʿba in prayer wherever on earth they may be.
rows.anchor: يعنى فحولوا وجوهكم فى الصلاة تلقاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Banu Salima’s mosque Muhammad had prayed one rakʿa when the qibla changed to the Kaʿba; fasting Ramadan, the qibla change, and prayer toward the Kaʿba were prescribed two months before Badr, and wine was forbidden before the Trench.
rows.anchor: كان النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلى فى مسجد بنى سلمة، فصلى ركعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Torah are Jews; al-Khamis ibn ʿAmr protested that the Kaʿba command was invented, prompting the reply that they know it is true.
rows.anchor: وهم اليهود، منهم الحميس بن عمرو، قال: يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews know that the Kaʿba is the true qibla from their Lord; their disbelief concerning the qibla is not hidden from God.
rows.anchor: بأن القبلة هى الكعبة، فأوعدهم الله، فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanhum ibn Sukayn, Rafiʿ ibn Sukayn, and Rafiʿ ibn Huraymila, along with Najran’s Christians al-Sayyid and al-ʿAqib, asked Muhammad for a prophetic sign.
rows.anchor: يعنى اليهود، ينحوم بن سكين، ورافع ابن سكين، ورافع ابن حريملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even with every sign, the People of the Book would not follow Muhammad’s Kaʿba qibla, and he would not follow their Jerusalem qibla.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولئن جئت يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews pray toward Jerusalem from the west and Christians from the east, so neither group follows the other’s qibla.
rows.anchor: إن اليهود يصلون قبل المغرب لبيت المقدس، والنصارى قبل المشرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil warns against following their desires and praying toward their qibla after receiving the clear explanation, which would make Muhammad a wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: فصليت إلى قبلتهم { من بعد ما جاءك من العلم } ، يعنى البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the first fasting rule, food, drink, and sex became forbidden after the night prayer or after sleeping before praying it, just as during the day.
rows.anchor: أن الرجل إذا صلى العشاء الآخرة، أو نام قبل أن يصليها، حرم عليه الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUmar had sex with his wife after praying ʿishāʾ, regretted it, and confessed to Muhammad, asking whether he could have a dispensation.
rows.anchor: عمر بن الخطاب، رضى الله عنه، صلى العشاء الآخرة، ثم جامع امرأته

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told ʿUmar he had not been justified in what he did; ʿUmar returned saddened.
rows.anchor: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم:لم تك جديرا بذلك يا عمر، فرجع حزينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarma ibn Anas worked in his garden, came home exhausted, fell asleep before eating, and woke to find food forbidden; he said fasting had worn him down.
rows.anchor: ورأى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم صرمة بن أنس بن صرمة بن مالك

words: فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Muslim men confessed to similar conduct and asked how to repent, God revealed the passage, assuring them of His nearness and response to prayer.
rows.anchor: واعترف رجال من المسلمين عند ذلك بما كانوا يصنعون بعد العشاء

words: فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is near in answering; “let them respond to Me” means obey, and “believe in Me” means affirm Him, so they may be guided.
rows.anchor: فليستجيبوا لى } بالطاعة، { وليؤمنوا بى

words: وَقَٰتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Hudaybiyya in Dhul-Qaʿda, 1,400 Muslims in pilgrimage garb were barred from the sanctuary and attacked by Meccans; God then permitted fighting.
rows.anchor: وأن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بينا هو وأصحابه معتمرون إلى مكة فى ذى القعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not initiate combat in the sacred month or sanctuary; beginning the fighting there would be transgression.
rows.anchor: فتبدأوا بقتالهم فى الشهر الحرام وفى الحرم، فإنه عدوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wherever you encounter them means anywhere, in or outside the sanctuary; expel them from Mecca because they expelled you from it.
rows.anchor: يعنى أين أدركتموهم فى الحل والحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna means shirk, a graver offense before God than killing; 9:49 likewise means they fell into unbelief.
rows.anchor: يعنى الشرك أعظم عند الله عز وجل جرما من القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A later prohibition on fighting anywhere in the sanctuary abrogated the earlier permission to kill opponents wherever found; fighting there was then allowed only if they attacked first.
rows.anchor: يعنى أرض الحرم كله، فنسخت هذه الآية، ثم رخص لهم

words: فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوْا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents stop fighting and affirm God’s oneness, He forgives their shirk and shows them mercy through Islam.
rows.anchor: عن قتالكم ووحدوا ربهم، { فإن الله غفور } لشركهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil links the command to fight until fitna ends with 8:39, explaining fitna as shirk and the goal as exclusive worship of God, especially among Arab polytheists.
rows.anchor: يقول: حتى لا يكون فيهم شرك فيوحدوا ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Religion for God” means the people worship and affirm Him alone, without worshipping anyone else.
rows.anchor: يعنى ويقوم { الدين لله } ، فيوحدوه ولا يعبدوا غيره

words: فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوْا۟ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stop shirk and affirm God’s oneness, there is no recourse except against wrongdoers who do not affirm Him alone.
rows.anchor: فلا عدوان } ، يعنى فلا سبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No recourse” means there is no way against someone; Muqatil supports this sense with the wording of 28:28.
rows.anchor:
فلا عدوان علي
[القصص: 28]، يعنى فلا سبيل على

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُۥ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who professed love for Muhammad and swore he would follow Islam; the Prophet welcomed him though his inward intent differed.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى الأخنس بن شريق بن عمرو بن وهب بن أبى سلمة الثقفى

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His appeal to God refers to his oath; he claimed that his words were true in his heart.
rows.anchor: يعنى يمينه التى حلف بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aldd al-khiṣām means arguing falsely; 19:97 likewise describes people as fiercely disputatious.
rows.anchor:
كقوله سبحانه:
وتنذر به قوما لدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When he leaves or disappears, this violent man pursues sins and corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: يعنى إذا توارى وكان رجلا مانعا جريئا على القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses the phrase as destroying every creature and reports that al-Akhnas burned a Muslim’s grain stack at Taif and killed his riding animal.
rows.anchor: يعنى كل دابة، وذلك أنه عمد إلى كديس بالطائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not love corruption.
rows.anchor: { والله لا يحب الفساد } [آية:205]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Pride seizes him through sin” means zeal; 38:2’s reference to pride and dissension likewise means sinful zeal.
rows.anchor:
نظيرها فى ص [آية: 2] قوله سبحانه:
بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell, with its severe punishment, is enough for him, and it is a wretched resting place.
rows.anchor: فحسبه جهنم } شدة عذاب، { ولبئس المهاد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akhnas was also called Ubayy ibn Shariq; he earned the name by turning back 300 Banu Zuhra men from Badr, arguing Muhammad was their nephew and should be spared whether truthful or false.
rows.anchor: وكان الأخنس يسمى أبى بن شريق، من بني زهرة بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divorced woman who menstruates waits for three menstrual periods; Muqatil takes qurūʾ to mean menstruations.
rows.anchor: يعنى ثلاث حيض إذا كانت ممن تحيض

words: وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God created in their wombs means a child; belief in God’s oneness and the resurrection entails not concealing it.
rows.anchor: يعنى يصدقن بالله بأنه واحد لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband has the stronger right to take his wife back while she is pregnant; the verse concerns Ismaʿil al-Ghifari and his wife, who did not know she was pregnant.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى إسماعيل الغفارى وفي امرأته لم تشعر بحبلها

words: وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ إِنْ أَرَادُوٓا۟ إِصْلَٰحًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For reconciliation, Ismaʿil revoked the divorce while his wife was pregnant; she gave birth, then she and the child died.
rows.anchor: فعمد إسماعيل فراجعها وهى حبلى، فولدت منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women have rights from their husbands corresponding to the rights their husbands have over them, in fairness.
rows.anchor: لهن من الحق على أزواجهن مثل ما لأزواجهن عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men have an advantage in rights over women; God is mighty and wise in His merciful ruling concerning pregnancy.
rows.anchor: يعنى حكم الرحمة عليها فى الحبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keep the five daily prayers at their appointed times.
rows.anchor: حافظوا على الصلوات } الخمس فى مواقيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle prayer is ʿaṣr.
rows.anchor: والصلاة الوسطى } ، يعنى صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qānitīn means obedient, as in 66:12, 16:120, and 4:34. Idolaters stand disobediently in prayer, while believers are told to obey.
rows.anchor: قانتين } [آية: 238] فى صلاتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In intense fear, pray two units on foot or mounted facing any possible direction; if unable to prostrate, nod with the head, make prostration lower than bowing, and place the forehead on nothing.
rows.anchor: يقول: على أرجلكم أو على دوابكم، فصلوا ركعتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once safe, remember God by praying, as He taught what people did not previously know.
rows.anchor: فاذكروا الله } ، يقول: فصلوا لله

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God requires a person to do only what that person is capable of doing.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا يكلفها من العمل إلا ما أطاقت

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person receives the good they earn and bears the sin they commit.
rows.anchor: من الخير وما عملت أو تظلمت به

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel taught Muhammad this plea: do not punish us for ignorance or error that made us leave God’s command; God answered, “That is granted to you.”
rows.anchor: يقول: إن جهلنا عن شىء أو أخطأنا، فتركنا أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣr means a covenant; the plea asks not to burden this community as God burdened Israel, forbidding camel meat, sheep fat, and all cloven-hoofed animals because of their sins, and making them apes and pigs.
rows.anchor: ما كان حرم عليهم من لحوم الإبل، وشحوم الغنم، ولحوم كل ذى ظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Pardon us” asks God to pardon, and “forgive us” asks Him to overlook all their sins.
rows.anchor: يقول: واعف عنا من ذلك، { واغفر لنا } ، يقول: وتجاوز عنا

words: أَنتَ مَوْلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is their protector; they ask victory over disbelievers of Mecca and elsewhere until Resurrection. God grants the requests, intercedes for the community, and exempts it for error, forgetfulness, and coercion, a favor withheld from earlier nations.
rows.anchor: يعنى كفار مكة وغيرها إلى يوم القيامة، قال الله تعالى: ذلك لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says God wrote a book on the Throne two thousand years before creating heaven and earth, sent down the final two verses of al-Baqara, and whoever recites them at home keeps Satan away for three days and nights.
rows.anchor: بلغنى أن الله عز وجل كتب كتابا قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض بألفى عام

words: مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil begins a report under the neighboring verse about lending God a good loan; its story continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن سليمان فى قوله

words: مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Dahdah asks Muhammad whether charity earns a garden in Paradise and whether his children and wife Umm al-Dahdah will accompany him; the Prophet answers yes.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الدحداح: يا رسول الله، إن تصدقت بصدقة، أفلى مثلها فى الجنة؟

words: مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He owns two gardens, al-Janna and al-Junayna, the latter better; he offers it to the poor as a loan to God and hesitates at its gate because he dedicated it.
rows.anchor: وكان له حديقتان، إحداهما تسمى الجنة، والأخرى الجنينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Dahdah calls to his wife in verse, celebrating the voluntary gift as a loan to God and hoping for multiplied reward in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: إلا رجاء الضعف فى الميعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm al-Dahdah calls the exchange profitable, accepts leaving with the children, and hands the garden to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فأجابته: ربح بيعك، والله لولا شرطك ما كان لك منه إلا مالك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet promises Abu al-Dahdah so many date palms in Paradise that all the people of Mina together could not lift one cluster.
rows.anchor: فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran, son of Mathan, was married to Hannah daughter of Faqudh, Mary’s mother; while pregnant, she vowed the child to God’s service if God saved her and she gave birth.
rows.anchor: بن ماثانا، اسمها حنة بنت فاقوز، وهى أم مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banu Mathan were Israelite kings descended from David; a consecrated child would avoid worldly work and marriage, serve the afterlife, and worship in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: وبنو ماثان من ملوك بنى إسرائيل من نسل داود، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only boys were consecrated in that era, so Hannah’s husband worried what she would do if the child were a girl, whom he called vulnerable; Hannah became concerned.
rows.anchor: لم يكن يحرر فى ذلك الزمان إلا الغلمان

words: فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّىٓ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hannah asks God to accept her vow; He hears their supplication and knows their vow.
rows.anchor: لدعائهما، العليم بنذرهما، يعنى بالتقبل والاستجابة لدعائهما

words: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍۢ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God nurtured Mary well in worship and obedience; Zechariah built her a chamber in Jerusalem’s temple, entered by ladder, and arranged a wet nurse.
rows.anchor: يقول: رباها تربية حسنة فى عبادة وطاعة لربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah locked Mary in, trusted no one else with her, brought her food and needs, took her to his home during menstruation, then returned her to the chamber when pure.
rows.anchor: فكان يغلق عليها الباب ومعه المفتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah saw grapes with Mary in the bitter winter; Gabriel had brought them from heaven.
rows.anchor: وكان زكريا يرى عندها العنب فى الشتاء الشديد البرد، فيأتيها به جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah asks where the out-of-season food came from; Mary says it is from God, who provides without measure to whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: يعنى من أين هذا فى غير حينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s out-of-season fruit leads Zechariah to hope God can restore his wife and grant a child; he asks for a pure, pious child, as in 19:6, and God answers although the couple are old.
rows.anchor: فطمع عند ذلك زكريا فى الولد

words: ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These events are unseen news revealed by God to Muhammad, who was not present when the people cast lots or disputed over Mary.
rows.anchor: يعنى حديثا من الغيب لم تشهده يا محمد

words: إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cast lots to decide who would take Mary into his care and later disputed over her guardianship.
rows.anchor: فى القرعة، { أيهم يكفل مريم } ، يعنى يضم مريم إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who turn away from faith in Muhammad after acknowledging him in the Torah are disobedient.
rows.anchor: يعنى فمن أعرض عن الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد إقراره، فى التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in the heavens who submit willingly are angels; those on earth are believers.
rows.anchor: يعنى الملائكة، { والأرض } ، يعنى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reluctant are adherents of other religions: they admit God is their Lord and Creator, yet remain polytheists.
rows.anchor: يعنى أهل الأديان، يقولون: الله هو ربهم، وهو خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone will return to God.
rows.anchor: وإليه يرجعون } [آية: 83]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides believers to laws of earlier believers, including marriage prohibitions by blood and in-law relations, and overlooks marriages made before the prohibition.
rows.anchor: يعنى شرائع هدى من كان قبلكم من المؤمنين من تحريم النسب والصهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those following desires are fornicators; Jews claimed that marrying a paternal half-sister’s daughter was lawful, turning far from truth.
rows.anchor: يعنى به الزنا، وذلك أن اليهود زعموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lightens the burden by allowing a man who cannot afford a free wife to marry a slave woman, so he does not fornicate.
rows.anchor: إذ رخص فى تزويج الأمة لمن لم يجد طولا لحرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are weak because they cannot patiently refrain from marriage; hence God permits marriage to slave women to prevent fornication.
rows.anchor: لا يصبر عن النكاح، ويضعف عن تركه، فلذلك أحل لهم تزويج الولائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd ibn al-Samin entrusted armor to Tuma ibn Ubayriq, who denied it and hid it in Abu Malik’s house; Tuma’s people framed Abu Malik and asked Muhammad to clear Tuma.
rows.anchor: ثم إن زيدا اليهودى طلب درعه فجحده طعمة، فقال زيد لقومه

words: لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān was sent down in truth, not in vain; Muhammad should judge by what God taught in scripture. Muqatil links the wording to 34:6.
rows.anchor: يعنى القرآن { بالحق } لم ننزله باطلا عبثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traitor for whom Muhammad must not argue is Tuma.
rows.anchor: خصيما } [آية: 105]، يعنى طعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad to seek forgiveness for arguing on Tuma’s behalf and falsely clearing him of theft; Muqatil says the Prophet sought forgiveness.
rows.anchor: يا محمد عن جدالك عن طعمة حين كذبت عنه، فأبرأته من السرقة

words: وَلَا تُجَٰدِلْ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who betray themselves refers to Tuma; God does not love a betrayer and sinner in his religion.
rows.anchor: أثيما } [آية: 107] فى دينه أثميا بربه

words: يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuma conceals his betrayal from people, but cannot conceal it from God.
rows.anchor: يعنى يستترون بالخيانة { من الناس } ، يعنى طعمة

words: وَهُوَ مَعَهُمْ إِذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرْضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Plot at night” means Qatada and Tuma’s companions devised what to tell the Prophet to defend him; God fully knows their deeds.
rows.anchor: يعنى إذ يؤلفون { ما لا يرضى من القول } ، لقولهم
